title: Boundary exceptional point driven chiral switch of topological edge states
abstract: We theoretically investigate the interplay of topology and localized non-Hermiticity in a finite Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain characterized by non-Hermitian potentials at its boundaries. By tuning the boundary gain and loss parameters, we exploit the finite-size hybridization of two mid-gap topological edge states to analytically derive the exact coordinates of boundary-induced exceptional points (EPs), $Γ_{\rm EP}=\pm i v^{N}/w^{N-1}$, at which these states undergo coalescence. We demonstrate that dynamically encircling these boundary EPs facilitates a robust, chiral edge state-transfer protocol. Depending on the orientation of the encircling loop, this protocol allows a topological edge state localized at one boundary to be either transferred to the opposite edge with perfect fidelity or returned to its starting position through a double switching process. Importantly, since the non-Hermiticity remains strictly confined to the boundaries, this chiral transport occurs without affecting the energy spectrum of the bulk bands. These results establish a minimal framework for a large-scale topological chiral switch that is experimentally verifiable and capable of being controlled through boundary non-Hermitian driving.
summary: The paper theoretically investigates controlling topological edge states in a finite SSH chain by introducing non-Hermitian potentials only at the boundaries. By dynamically encircling the resulting exceptional points, the system achieves a robust, chiral state-transfer protocol. This method allows for directional pumping of edge excitations without perturbing the bulk energy spectrum, offering a blueprint for topological quantum switches.
main_problem: To establish a minimal, experimentally verifiable framework for a large-scale topological chiral switch using boundary non-Hermiticity while ensuring the bulk energy spectrum remains unperturbed.
main_result: Dynamically encircling boundary-induced exceptional points (EPs) facilitates a robust, chiral edge state-transfer protocol, allowing unidirectional state transfer between opposite edges.
method: The study analytically derives EP coordinates and uses time-dependent Schrödinger equation simulations to track state populations during closed parameter loops.
model_or_system: The system is a finite Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain lattice modeled by a Hamiltonian $H = H_{	ext{bulk}} + H_{	ext{boundary}}(t)$, where non-Hermiticity is confined to the boundaries.
key_observables: Normalized site populations ($P_{	ext{left}}, P_{	ext{right}}$), the dynamical energy $E(t)$, and the transfer fidelity.
important_parameters: The hopping amplitudes ($v, w$), the non-Hermitian gain/loss parameters ($\gamma(t)$), and the loop chirality ($\circlearrowright$ vs $\circlearrowleft$).
main_assumptions: The non-Hermiticity is strictly confined to the boundaries, and the bulk Hamiltonian $H_{	ext{bulk}}$ is strictly Hermitian.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the splitting of edge state energies ($E_+, E_-$), the time evolution of site populations during chiral switching, and the complex trajectory of the dynamical energy on Riemann surfaces.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the non-Hermitian SSH model and deriving EP locations to simulating the state transfer protocol by dynamically encircling these EPs, demonstrating chiral control.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, controllable mechanism for topological state manipulation using boundary engineering, which is highly relevant for designing robust quantum devices in open quantum systems.
